Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 34 (CoreSite missing-address campaign): added a two-source-corroborated aggregator address and square footage, flagged a conflicting single-source street number rather than silently resolving it, no MW figure available. research_status remains complete.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CoreSite was founded in 2001 as CRG West, a Carlyle Group portfolio company, beginning operations at two West Coast carrier hotel buildings, Market Post Tower and One Wilshire, both in Los Angeles. The firm rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009 and completed an IPO in September 2010. American Tower Corporation, the public tower and infrastructure company (NYSE: AMT, SEC CIK 1053507), completed its acquisition of CoreSite in December 2021. Stonepeak Partners LP later bought roughly 29 percent of American Towers US data center business directly in July 2022, increasing that stake to about 36 percent by October 2022. CoreSites own current Silicon Valley regional page (operator source, tier-1, https://www.coresite.com/data-center-locations/silicon-valley) names nine data centers on this Santa Clara campus, SV1 through SV9, totaling more than 1.4 million square feet campus wide, but only describes SV1, SV2, SV4, SV7, SV8, and SV9 individually, SV1 and SV2 are not rows in this registry. SV3, SV5, and SV6 are not detailed on that page, so their building specific facts below come from data center industry aggregator directories instead. This specific building, SV5, is one of the three Silicon Valley buildings the operators own regional page names but does not detail individually. Baxtel and Ocolo independently agree this buildings address is 2900 Stender Way, Santa Clara, CA, Ocolo further gives 101,430 square feet. A separate DataCenterMap listing shows a conflicting street number, 2950 Stender Way, apparently for the same building. Since two independent aggregators agree on 2900 and only one shows 2950, the 2900 figure is treated as more likely correct, but this conflict is noted rather than silently resolved. No MW or power capacity figure was found for this specific building in any source checked this session.

reading.body:
CoreSite SV5 is a 101,430 square foot building on the nine-building Santa Clara campus that CoreSite owns in Silicon Valley. The operator does not publish power capacity for this specific building, and no figure appears in industry aggregators either. Without watts, the scale of its AI hosting potential cannot be assessed from published data.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities, of which 11 publish power capacity totaling 365 MW. CoreSite's Santa Clara campus as a whole ranks 12th by published capacity statewide, but the operator does not break down power by building within the campus, leaving SV5's contribution to that ranking unknown.

SV5 is one of three buildings on the campus that CoreSite names but does not detail individually on its regional page, making it invisible to the operator's own public specifications. Any assessment of whether this facility matters to AI infrastructure requires either the operator to publish its power capacity or independent measurement, neither of which is available in current sources.
